newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MCCARRON JOINS DUVAL IN LEAD AT ATLANTA CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MCCARRON JOINS DUVAL IN LEAD AT ATLANTA CLASSIC.

text.p: Long-hitting Scott McCarron, playing with a pulled hamstring, coped with a testing breeze to join David Duval in the lead after the third round of the $1.5 million BellSouth Atlanta Classic Saturday.

"The wind was really swirling. It was tough to pick the right club. I guessed right quite a few times and hit the ball pretty well," McCarron said after compiling seven birdies in a six-under-par 66, the day's lowest round on the new Sugarloaf course.
Halfway pacesetter Duval bogeyed the final hole to shoot 73 and stand with McCarron at 11-under 205 with one round to play, two strokes ahead of fellow American David Toms (70).
Bill Glasson (69) was three shots back, along with Zimbabwe's Nick Price (75), who finished poorly with a double bogey at the 15th and a bogey at the 17th.
Course designer and world number one Greg Norman also endured a frustrating day. He failed to capitalise on three early birdies on his way to a 73 that left him five strokes adrift.

McCarron, who has one PGA Tour victory, has the second-best third-round scoring average on tour this year. "I've played really well on Saturdays this year, and that's due to the fact my wife is making me stay in Friday nights now in the hotel room," he quipped.
"I've got a little more confidence than I did a year and a half ago, so I feel I belong and that's a big key."
McCarron pulled his left hamstring during Friday's second round when he was sprinting to mark his ball on the 11th hole after play had been stopped due to bad weather.
He was sprinting because Dicky Pride, with whom he was playing, challenged him to a race down the fairway. "We took off in a full sprint and about 60 yards out I heard something pop," McCarron said.

"Now it just feels like a big cramp back there. I told Dicky I'm going to dedicate this tournament to him because I think it's keeping my swing slower. I'm not able to go after the ball as hard as I normally do and I've got to walk a bit slower too."
Co-leader Duval, who has finished second six times without winning on the PGA Tour, tried to play down the pressure he inevitably feels to win.
"I've given myself a chance to win. Anytime you do that you have to feel good about your game. I'm not going to let the bogey on the last hole bother me," he said.
